question: Who was Samuel's firstborn son?
summary: 1 Samuel 8:2 names Samuel's firstborn son as Joel and his second son as Abijah. 1 Chronicles 6:28 in the Masoretic Hebrew names the firstborn as 'Vashni' and the second as Abijah. The two genealogies disagree on the name of Samuel's eldest son.

reconcile.connective: Commentators across the tradition read “Vashni” not as a name but as a copyist’s corruption of Hebrew vesheni (“and the second”), with Joel’s name dropped from the Chronicles text.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, listing this in the Skeptic’s Annotated Bible, presses the bare conflict—Joel in 1 Samuel 8:2 against “Vashni” in the King James 1 Chronicles 6:28—though the discrepancy rests on a Masoretic reading the critical apparatus treats as a scribal error.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); contradiction page “Who was Samuel's firstborn son?” (skepticsannotatedbible.com)

pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, arguing 'Vashni' is a corruption of vesheni ('the second') and that 'Joel' dropped from the Hebrew, with the Syriac and Arabic preserving the original reading of 1 Samuel 8:2.

excerpts.excerpt_text: It is now generally thought by the best critics that, through an error of the copyists, an omission has been made of the oldest son’s name, and that Vashni, which is not the name of a person, merely signifies “and the second.” This critical emendation of the text makes all clear, as well as consistent with other passages relating to the family of Samuel.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the Joel/Vashni tension: Vashni is not a name but a corruption of 'and the second,' with the firstborn's name dropped by a copyist.
excerpts.source_note_text: the sons of Samuel--The sons of Samuel are here named Vashni and Abiah. The first-born is called Joel (Sa1 8:2); and this name is given to him in Ch1 6:33. It is now generally thought by the best critics that, through an error of the copyists, an omission has been made of the oldest son's name, and that Vashni, which is not the name of a person, merely signifies "and the second." This critical emendation of the text makes all clear, as well as consistent with other passages relating to the family of Samuel.
